newsitem.title: TAIWAN: ADB may issue 3rd Taiwan dlr-bonds -central banker.
newsitem.headline: ADB may issue 3rd Taiwan dlr-bonds -central banker.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank may issue Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in Taiwan later in 1997 for the third time, a central bank official on Friday quoted central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong as saying.

"The ADB may issue Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in Taiwan later this year for the third time," the official quoted Sheu as saying late on Thursday when he returned from an annual Asian Development Bank meeting in Japan.
But the amount has yet to be set, Sheu was quoted as saying.
In December 1996, the ADB issued T$7 billion, or US$255 million worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds.
The central bank had said the ADB's planned bond issue would help internationalise Taiwan's bond market and raise the credibility of Taiwan's currency.
The ADB also planned to come to the island to hold presentations for ADB-led or -financed international syndicated loans and purchases, Sheu was quoted as saying.
The central bank had said the ADB would help Taiwan firms strive for international bids of ADB-financed development projects.
Taiwan is a member of the ADB.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million.
